introduction: The `afspec` Go validation module completes the validation pipeline for the Go port of the `afspec` library, implementing all cross-file integrity rules, cross-spec rules, and warning categories to achieve parity with the Python reference implementation.

glossary.DependencyEdge: A directed edge in the DependencyGraph connecting an upstream spec to a downstream spec.
glossary.DependencyGraph: Go struct representing the directed graph of spec dependencies, used by cross-spec validation.
glossary.Schemas: Function returning a map of embedded JSON Schema file bytes used for schema validation.
glossary.Validate: Method on *Spec that combines schema, cross-file, and warning checks into a ValidationResult.
glossary.ValidateCrossFile: Method on *Spec that checks cross-file integrity rules (e.g. property test coverage, glossary terms, traceability deduplication), returning a slice of ValidationEntry.
glossary.ValidateCrossSpec: Package-level function that checks cross-spec rules across a map of specs and a DependencyGraph, returning a slice of ValidationEntry.
glossary.ValidateSchema: Method on *Spec that runs JSON Schema and EARS pattern checks, returning a slice of ValidationEntry.
glossary.ValidateStructured: Method on *Spec that returns a map[string]any with keys 'errors', 'warnings', and 'valid' for structured output consumption.
glossary.ValidationEntry: Go struct with fields Category, Message, Artifact, Path, Keyword, Check, RequirementID, EntityID string and Value any representing a single validation finding.
glossary.ValidationResult: Go struct with fields Valid bool, Errors []ValidationEntry, Warnings []ValidationEntry representing the outcome of a full validation run.
glossary.backtick term: A term enclosed in backtick characters within a criterion or property field, which must have a corresponding glossary entry.
glossary.boundary coverage: A smoke test that exercises the interface between two specs connected by a dependency edge, ensuring the integration point is tested.
glossary.checkMissingSubtaskRefs: Package-level function in validate_missing_refs.go that checks for subtasks with empty test_spec_refs or requirement_refs.
glossary.correctness_property: A formal invariant defined in the requirements artifact that must hold for all valid inputs, linked to property-based tests via property_id.
glossary.ears_pattern: The EARS (Easy Approach to Requirements Syntax) pattern type of a criterion: ubiquitous, event_driven, complex_event, state_driven, unwanted, or optional.
glossary.execution_path: A named sequence of actor-action steps in the requirements artifact tracing a user-visible feature from entry point to observable side effect.
glossary.execution_path_id: The identifier on a smoke_test entry that links it to a specific execution_path.
glossary.property_id: The identifier on a property_test entry that links it to a specific correctness_property.
glossary.property_test: A test_spec entry that validates a correctness_property via property-based testing, matched by property_id.
glossary.requirement_refs: A list of requirement or criterion IDs on a subtask, linking implementation tasks to the requirements they implement.
glossary.return_contract: The caller-observable result of a criterion action, such as a return value, HTTP status, or error type.
glossary.smoke_test: A test_spec entry that validates an execution_path end-to-end, matched by execution_path_id.
glossary.test_spec_id: An identifier referencing a specific test entry (test_case, property_test, edge_case_test, or smoke_test) in the test_spec artifact.
glossary.test_spec_refs: A list of test_spec_id values on a subtask, linking implementation tasks to their covering tests.
glossary.traceability: The set of entries mapping requirement IDs to test_spec_ids, establishing coverage linkage between requirements and tests.
glossary.vague language: Words such as 'appropriate', 'properly', 'correctly', 'adequate', or 'sufficient' in criterion fields that reduce testability.
glossary.wiring_verification: A task group kind whose subtasks verify that all implementation stubs are replaced and all smoke tests pass end-to-end.

user_story.goal: have the validator flag any correctness_property that lacks a corresponding property_test
user_story.benefit: I can ensure every formal invariant is covered by a property-based test before shipping

acceptance_criteria.action: check that each correctness_property has a matching property_test in test_spec (matched by property_id); for each unmatched property, append a ValidationEntry with Category='integrity', the uncovered property ID in RequirementID, and a descriptive Message
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns []ValidationEntry containing one entry per uncovered correctness_property; returns empty slice when all properties are covered
acceptance_criteria.trigger: ValidateCrossFile is called on a Spec whose requirements contain one or more correctness_properties

acceptance_criteria.action: set the Path field of each property-coverage ValidationEntry to the JSON path of the uncovered correctness_property within the requirements artifact

edge_cases.action: skip property test coverage checks and produce no integrity errors for this rule
edge_cases.return_contract: returns empty slice for this rule
edge_cases.trigger: ValidateCrossFile is called on a Spec with no correctness_properties

edge_cases.action: treat all correctness_properties as uncovered and produce one error per property
edge_cases.return_contract: returns []ValidationEntry with one entry per correctness_property
edge_cases.trigger: ValidateCrossFile is called on a Spec with no test_spec

edge_cases.action: treat the correctness_property as covered (no error) regardless of duplicates
edge_cases.return_contract: returns no error for that property_id
edge_cases.trigger: multiple property_tests share the same property_id

requirements.title: Execution path smoke test coverage rule (cross-file rule 4)

user_story.benefit: I can ensure every user-visible flow is covered by an end-to-end smoke test

acceptance_criteria.action: check that each execution_path has a matching smoke_test in test_spec (matched by execution_path_id); for each unmatched path, append a ValidationEntry with Category='integrity' and a descriptive Message identifying the uncovered execution_path_id
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns []ValidationEntry containing one entry per uncovered execution_path; returns empty slice when all paths are covered
acceptance_criteria.trigger: ValidateCrossFile is called on a Spec whose requirements contain one or more execution_paths

edge_cases.action: skip smoke test coverage checks and produce no integrity errors for this rule
edge_cases.return_contract: returns empty slice for this rule
edge_cases.trigger: ValidateCrossFile is called on a Spec with no execution_paths

edge_cases.action: treat all execution_paths as uncovered and produce one error per path
edge_cases.return_contract: returns []ValidationEntry with one entry per execution_path
edge_cases.trigger: ValidateCrossFile is called on a Spec with execution_paths but no test_spec

user_story.goal: have the validator flag any test_spec_id in traceability or subtask refs that does not resolve to a known test entry
user_story.benefit: I can catch broken test references before they cause silent coverage gaps

acceptance_criteria.action: build a set of all known test IDs from test_spec (test_case, property_test, edge_case_test, smoke_test entries); for each test_spec_id in traceability entries and each entry in subtask test_spec_refs, check membership in that set; for each unresolvable ID, append a ValidationEntry with Category='integrity' and the unresolvable ID in the Message
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns []ValidationEntry with one entry per unresolvable test_spec_id; returns empty slice when all IDs resolve
acceptance_criteria.trigger: ValidateCrossFile is called on a Spec with traceability entries or subtask test_spec_refs

edge_cases.action: produce a separate error for each occurrence (traceability and subtask ref are checked independently)
edge_cases.return_contract: returns two ValidationEntry values for the same unresolvable ID
edge_cases.trigger: a test_spec_id appears in both a traceability entry and a subtask test_spec_refs and is unresolvable

edge_cases.action: skip test_spec_id resolution checks and produce no errors for this rule
edge_cases.return_contract: returns empty slice for this rule
edge_cases.trigger: ValidateCrossFile is called on a Spec with no traceability and no subtask test_spec_refs

user_story.goal: have the validator flag any backtick-wrapped term in criterion or property fields that lacks a glossary entry
user_story.benefit: I can ensure all domain-specific terms are defined and the spec is self-contained

acceptance_criteria.action: extract all backtick-wrapped terms from criterion fields (action, trigger, condition, error_condition, state, feature) and correctness property fields (for_any, invariant) using a package-level compiled regex; exclude terms that are numeric (including negatives and decimals), single characters, quoted strings (wrapped in single or double quotes), or longer than 80 characters; for each remaining term not present in the spec's glossary, append a ValidationEntry with Category='integrity' identifying the term and its source field
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns []ValidationEntry with one entry per missing glossary term; returns empty slice when all backtick terms are defined
acceptance_criteria.trigger: ValidateCrossFile is called on a Spec

acceptance_criteria.action: compile the backtick extraction regex at package initialization time (not inside the function body) to avoid repeated compilation overhead

edge_cases.action: produce one error per occurrence (each field reference is checked independently)
edge_cases.return_contract: returns one ValidationEntry per missing-term occurrence
edge_cases.trigger: a backtick term appears in multiple criterion fields across multiple requirements

edge_cases.action: exclude the term from glossary checks and produce no error for it
edge_cases.return_contract: returns no error for excluded numeric terms

edge_cases.action: exclude the term from glossary checks and produce no error for it

edge_cases.action: exclude the term from glossary checks and produce no error for it

edge_cases.trigger: a backtick term is longer than 80 characters

edge_cases.action: treat every non-excluded backtick term as missing and produce one error per term occurrence

user_story.goal: have the validator flag duplicate (requirement_id, test_spec_id) pairs in traceability
user_story.benefit: I can keep traceability data clean and avoid misleading coverage counts

requirements.title: Cross-spec duplicate API symbol rule (cross-spec rule 1)

user_story.goal: have the validator flag mismatched API symbol signatures between connected specs
user_story.benefit: I can catch interface contract drift between specs before it causes integration failures

acceptance_criteria.action: for each pair of specs connected by a DependencyEdge, compare their external_apis entries; for each symbol name that appears in both specs, check that the signature fields match; for each mismatch, append a ValidationEntry with Category='integrity' identifying the symbol name, the two specs, and the differing signatures
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns []ValidationEntry with one entry per mismatched symbol; returns empty slice when all shared symbols have matching signatures
acceptance_criteria.trigger: ValidateCrossSpec is called with a map of specs and a DependencyGraph containing dependency edges

edge_cases.action: skip duplicate API symbol checks and produce no errors for this rule
edge_cases.return_contract: returns empty slice for this rule

requirements.title: Cross-spec interface contract mismatch rule (cross-spec rule 4)

user_story.goal: have the validator flag return_contract mismatches between upstream and downstream specs for shared symbols
user_story.benefit: I can ensure downstream specs consume upstream interfaces with the correct expected return types

acceptance_criteria.action: extract backtick-wrapped terms from criterion action fields paired with their return_contract values; along each DependencyEdge, if a downstream spec's criterion references a symbol that an upstream spec also defines with a return_contract, compare the contracts; for each mismatch, append a ValidationEntry with Category='integrity' identifying the symbol, the two specs, and the differing contracts

edge_cases.return_contract: returns no error when both sides have null return_contract for the symbol

requirements.title: Cross-spec missing boundary coverage rule (cross-spec rule 5)

correctness_properties.title: Property test coverage completeness
correctness_properties.for_any: Spec with N correctness_properties and a test_spec with M property_tests
correctness_properties.invariant: ValidateCrossFile returns exactly one integrity error per correctness_property whose property_id does not appear in any property_test entry

correctness_properties.title: Smoke test coverage completeness
correctness_properties.for_any: Spec with N execution_paths and a test_spec with M smoke_tests
correctness_properties.invariant: ValidateCrossFile returns exactly one integrity error per execution_path whose execution_path_id does not appear in any smoke_test entry

correctness_properties.title: Backtick term exclusion correctness
correctness_properties.for_any: any backtick-wrapped term extracted from a criterion or property field
correctness_properties.invariant: the term is excluded from glossary checks if and only if it is numeric (including negatives and decimals), a single character, a quoted string, or longer than 80 characters

correctness_properties.title: Traceability pair uniqueness
correctness_properties.for_any: Spec with any number of traceability entries
correctness_properties.invariant: ValidateCrossFile returns exactly N-1 errors for any (requirement_id, test_spec_id) pair that appears N times (N > 1), and zero errors for pairs that appear exactly once

correctness_properties.title: ValidateStructured valid flag consistency
correctness_properties.invariant: the 'valid' field in the ValidateStructured output is true if and only if the 'errors' slice is empty

correctness_properties.title: Warning threshold strictness
correctness_properties.invariant: warning rules for group test_spec_refs (>15), group subtask count (>6), and subtask test_spec_refs (>8) produce no warning at exactly the threshold value and exactly one warning at threshold+1

correctness_properties.title: Unwanted pattern error completeness
correctness_properties.invariant: ValidateCrossFile returns exactly one integrity error for each criterion with ears_pattern='unwanted' and a null or empty return_contract, and zero errors for unwanted criteria with a non-empty return_contract

execution_paths.title: Full cross-file validation run on a spec with all rule violations

steps.action: calls ValidateCrossFile on a Spec that violates all 7 cross-file rules
runs property test coverage check (rule 3) and appends errors for uncovered properties
runs smoke test coverage check (rule 4) and appends errors for uncovered paths
runs test_spec_id resolution check (rule 5) and appends errors for unresolvable IDs
runs glossary backtick term check (rule 6) and appends errors for undefined terms
runs traceability deduplication check (rule 8) and appends errors for duplicate pairs
runs requirement_refs resolution check (rule 9) and appends errors for unresolvable refs
runs unwanted return_contract check (rule 10) and appends errors for missing contracts
returns the combined []ValidationEntry slice to the caller

execution_paths.title: ValidateStructured call producing structured JSON-compatible output

steps.action: calls ValidateStructured on a Spec
calls Validate internally to obtain ValidationResult with Errors and Warnings
maps each ValidationEntry in Errors to a map[string]any with category, rule, message, file, and path fields
maps each ValidationEntry in Warnings to a map[string]any with message and entity_id fields
sets 'valid' to true if Errors is empty, false otherwise
returns the assembled map[string]any to the caller

execution_paths.title: Cross-spec validation run detecting API symbol mismatch and unknown dependency

steps.action: calls ValidateCrossSpec with a map of specs and a DependencyGraph
iterates over DependencyEdge pairs and compares external API symbol signatures for shared symbol names
appends integrity errors for each mismatched signature
iterates over all specs and checks depends_on_spec values against the spec map keys
appends integrity errors for each unknown depends_on_spec reference
returns the combined []ValidationEntry slice to the caller

execution_paths.title: Full Validate run producing warnings for a large spec

steps.action: calls Validate on a Spec with 11 requirements, a group with 7 subtasks, and vague language in criteria
calls ValidateSchema and ValidateCrossFile to collect errors
runs scope limit warning check and appends a warning for more than 10 requirements
runs group subtask count warning check and appends a warning for the group with 7 subtasks
runs vague language check and appends warnings for each vague term found
returns ValidationResult with Valid=false (if errors exist) or Valid=true, plus all collected Warnings

error_handling.condition: ValidateCrossFile encounters a nil Spec pointer
error_handling.behavior: returns an empty []ValidationEntry immediately without panicking; the caller receives a zero-length slice
skips all edge-dependent rules (rules 1, 4, 5) and processes only non-edge rules; returns errors only for rules that do not require graph traversal

error_handling.condition: ValidateCrossSpec receives a nil or empty spec map
error_handling.behavior: returns an empty []ValidationEntry immediately without panicking

error_handling.condition: backtick extraction regex fails to compile at package initialization
error_handling.behavior: causes a package-level init panic with a descriptive message; this is a programming error and must be caught during development, not at runtime

error_handling.condition: vague language regex fails to compile at package initialization
error_handling.behavior: causes a package-level init panic with a descriptive message; this is a programming error and must be caught during development, not at runtime

error_handling.condition: ValidateStructured is called on a Spec that produces validation errors
error_handling.behavior: returns a map with 'valid' set to false and 'errors' containing all ValidationEntry maps; does not panic or return nil
